findings.title: Cache-before-DB lets blocked devices bypass device limit on retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI in AnonDeviceService inserts the device CacheKey into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice, and returns nil immediately on cache hit without touching the DB. When the limit is reached the first TagDevice for a new device returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and denies auth, but the key stays cached. The next request for the same blocked device hits the cache, returns success, and anonymous auth is allowed. The limit therefore only blocks the first request per 29-minute cache window.

findings.title: Count-then-insert race allows exceeding device limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit with a separate CountDevices query followed by an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT/ON DUPLICATE KEY if count is below the limit, otherwise an UPDATE. There is no transaction, lock, or unique-count constraint between the check and the insert. Two concurrent requests for different new devices can both observe count below the limit and both insert, permanently exceeding the configured limit.

findings.title: Anonymous auth now blocks synchronously on device tagging with no timeout
findings.body: Authenticate previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout using a detached context, so slow DB never blocked login. This change calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context with no timeout, and TagDevice now does a COUNT plus an upsert when a limit is configured. Every cache-miss anonymous login now pays that DB latency, and a slow or hung DB will stall anonymous authentication instead of being best-effort.

findings.title: No test that existing devices can still update after limit reached
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only verifies that a second distinct device is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached when the limit is 1. It never verifies the intended allowed path that an already-counted device within the 30-day window can still be updated via updateDevice when the limit is reached. A regression breaking updates for existing devices while blocking new ones would not be caught.
